text: Recursion is when a function calls itself to solve a smaller piece of the same problem.
Every recursion needs a base case — a stopping point. For factorial, that's when n reaches one.
Otherwise it multiplies n by the factorial of n minus one, shrinking the problem each step.
[chuckle] So factorial of five quietly becomes five times four times three times two times one.
The classic fibonacci is recursive too — each number is the sum of the two before it.
Its base case returns n directly when n is zero or one, stopping the chain.
[sniff] Where recursion truly shines is walking nested structures, like a list inside a list inside a list.
deep_sum checks each item — if it's a list, it recurses into it; otherwise it just adds the number.
So it flattens and totals any depth of nesting without you knowing the shape in advance.
[groan] Just always give recursion a base case — without one, it calls itself forever and crashes.
